clue.text: Computer record incorporating a note to read further

indicators.note: incorporating means the record takes the following letters into its middle

parts.note: LP is a long-playing record
taken as written
PTO, 'please turn over', is the note at the foot of a page telling you to read on

explanation.surface: A computer file that contains a reminder to keep reading.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Computer record' reads as one phrase, but the definition is just 'Computer'; PTO is the note printed at the foot of a page.
explanation.definitionFit: A portable personal machine is one kind of computer, so this is an example of the class.

clue.text: Deserted site gathering interest as artistic quarter

parts.note: left means deserted, abandoned
a bank is where deposits earn interest

explanation.surface: An abandoned site gains attention as a district for artists.
explanation.definitionFit: The south side of the Seine in Paris is famous as a quarter of painters and writers.

clue.text: Standard weapon in a manner of speaking

parts.note: par is the standard or normal level
a lance is a weapon

explanation.surface: Calling something a standard weapon is just a figure of speech.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a particular way of using language, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Correct without marks exam

indicators.note: without means the marks letter is taken away

parts.note: moral means correct, ethically right
M is the abbreviation for marks, the old German currency

explanation.surface: A correct exam that has no marks on it.
explanation.definitionFit: A spoken test, as in a language exam, is a kind of examination.

clue.text: A paper having liberal line over period despite everything

indicators.note: over here means the liberal and line come after the period, finishing the word

parts.note: taken as written
FT is the Financial Times newspaper
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: A newspaper with a liberal editorial line, lasting over some period, persists regardless.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom meaning nevertheless, in spite of all that has happened.

clue.text: Rum chief in TA's drunk as a pub staple?

indicators.note: drunk means unsteady, so the letters stagger into a new order

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army; the 's is the link 'is'

explanation.surface: The commanding officer of the Territorial Army is drunk on rum in a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: The Territorial Army (TA) is Britain's reserve force. A fruit machine is a coin-operated gambling machine found in many British pubs.
explanation.definitionFit: A coin-operated gaming machine is a common fixture in British pubs, hence a staple.

clue.text: City house? 'City house!'

parts.note: EC is the postcode for the City of London

explanation.surface: Someone asks about a house in the City and the phrase comes back at them.
explanation.walkthrough: The second 'City house' repeats the first, which is the definition: a repetition.
explanation.definitionFit: A reverberation repeating a sound is exactly what the repeated phrase represents.

clue.text: State admitting duke and bishop regularly, say

indicators.note: admitting means letting the duke in, so his letter goes inside

parts.note: to aver is to state
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A state regularly admits dukes and bishops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' looks like an instruction to take alternate letters, but with 'say' it is an example of the word class.
explanation.definitionFit: A word modifying a verb, like 'regularly', belongs to this part of speech.

clue.text: Pound yielding less in East End store

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for pound sterling

indicators.note: Cockney speech of London's East End drops the H at the start of words

parts.note: harder means giving way less, less yielding

explanation.surface: A pound gives a poorer return in an East End shop.
explanation.walkthrough: The East End is the traditionally working-class area of London where Cockney is spoken, famous for dropping H.
explanation.definitionFit: A pantry or cupboard for keeping food is a place of storage.

clue.text: Style of programme suitable to partner mostly

parts.note: something made for children is suitable to them, so FOR

indicators.note: mostly means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a mate is a partner

explanation.surface: A broadcaster chooses a show style that suits a partner.
explanation.definitionFit: A television show's format is its fixed structure and style, a standard broadcasting sense.

clue.text: Effort completed for walk in the park

parts.note: a push is an effort
something completed is over

explanation.surface: A finished effort that turned out to be easy.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are idioms for a task needing no real effort, something easily done.

clue.text: Habits harder to change in small measure

indicators.note: to change means to alter, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Habits become harder to change, bit by bit.
explanation.definitionFit: The width of a single strand of hair, idiomatically a tiny margin or distance.

clue.text: Tired officer's area to patrol

definitions.meaning: the round a police officer walks regularly

explanation.surface: A policeman worn out by walking his patch.
explanation.definitionFit: One word means exhausted in slang and also names a constable's regular round.

clue.text: Social and political organisation

definitions.meaning: a social is a gathering or get-together
a group such as Labour or the Conservatives contesting elections

explanation.surface: A body that is both a social club and a political group.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a festive gathering and also an organised group seeking political power.

clue.text: Cheese not lasting long, fine to ignore

indicators.note: to ignore means the fine letter is left out of the word

parts.note: something brief does not last long
F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A soft cheese that goes off quickly, too good to pass up.
explanation.definitionFit: A soft French cow's-milk cheese named after its region, an example of the class.

clue.text: Worth found in former itinerary

indicators.note: found in means the letters lie inside the run of words

explanation.surface: Something valuable discovered on an old travel plan.
explanation.definitionFit: Excellence or value deserving recognition is a synonym of worth.

clue.text: A vet's arranged place for notes

indicators.note: arranged means put in a new order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters A, V, E, T, S, with the possessive S counted

explanation.surface: A vet sets out a spot for leaving messages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'notes' suggests memos, but these are musical notes.
explanation.definitionFit: The set of five lines where music is written, another name for a staff.

clue.text: Foreign character creates law for regulating hazardous material

parts.note: nu is a letter of the Greek alphabet

indicators.note: regulating means putting into a new order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An outsider writes a law to control dangerous substances.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Foreign character' means a letter of a non-Roman alphabet, here Greek.
explanation.definitionFit: Spent radioactive fuel and by-products are a dangerous substance needing careful disposal.

clue.text: Woman's instant control in plane

parts.note: Joy is a woman's name, with the possessive S
a tick is an instant, a moment

explanation.surface: A woman takes the controls of an aircraft at once.
explanation.definitionFit: The lever a pilot moves to steer an aircraft is its control column.

clue.text: Perhaps mandarin number one's given rise for achievement

parts.note: a mandarin orange is an example of fruit

indicators.note: given rise means the letters go upward, read backwards in this down clue

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A Chinese official, the top man, gets promoted for his success.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mandarin' suggests a Chinese official but is the citrus fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: Realisation of a plan, its coming to completion, is an achievement.

clue.text: Impropriety and hubris a movie dissected

indicators.note: dissected means cut apart, so the letters are taken to pieces and rearranged

explanation.surface: A critic picks apart a film about arrogance and bad conduct.
explanation.definitionFit: Improper behaviour, bad conduct, is a direct synonym of impropriety.

clue.text: Bike not made for touring over passes

indicators.note: touring means travelling round, so the letters are moved about
passes means the over letter goes away, leaving the rest

parts.note: O is the cricket abbreviation for over

explanation.surface: A bicycle unsuited to touring over mountain passes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'touring' rearranges NOT MADE, and 'passes' takes O out of it, leaving the letters of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A bicycle built for two riders, one behind the other, is a kind of bike.

clue.text: Motive concerning crime devoid of right

parts.note: re means concerning, about

indicators.note: devoid of means the right letter is taken out

parts.note: arson is a crime

explanation.surface: A detective seeks the motive for a crime with no justification.
explanation.definitionFit: A cause or ground for an action is its motive, a synonym.

clue.text: Top copy, ten required

parts.note: to ape is to copy
X is the Roman numeral for ten

explanation.surface: An office asks for ten copies of the top sheet.
explanation.definitionFit: The highest point or peak of something is its summit, a synonym of top.

clue.text: Plant close to fence devoured by small horse

indicators.note: devoured by means the letter ends up inside the horse

parts.note: a pony is a small horse

indicators.note: close to means the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: A pony eats a plant growing by the fence.
explanation.definitionFit: A showy flowering garden shrub, an example of a plant.

clue.text: What goes into Genoa's tipple?

indicators.note: goes into means the letters sit inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A question about what an Italian city drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: The word straddles 'Genoa's' and 'tipple', and is itself an Italian wine one might drink in Genoa.
explanation.definitionFit: A sparkling white wine from Piedmont, so plausibly a drink in a northern Italian city.

clue.text: Sound of a queen maybe, largely untainted queen

indicators.note: largely means most of the word, losing its last letter

parts.note: pure means untainted
R is the abbreviation for queen, from Regina

explanation.surface: A royal sound, mostly from an unblemished monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'queen' is a female cat, not a monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: The contented rumble a cat makes, and a queen is a female cat.

clue.text: Singer that's enthusiastic on the up

indicators.note: on the up means going upward, read backwards in this down clue

parts.note: avid means enthusiastic

explanation.surface: A keen singer whose career is rising.
explanation.definitionFit: A celebrated female opera singer is a prima donna, a kind of singer.

clue.text: Deter daughter getting publicity in publication

indicators.note: in means the publicity goes inside the publication

parts.note: an issue is an edition of a magazine
an ad is publicity

explanation.surface: A daughter appears in a magazine feature to discourage others.
explanation.definitionFit: To discourage someone from acting is to deter them, a synonym.

clue.text: Most of what riders do with one or two items of beachwear

indicators.note: most of means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: cyclists or motorcyclists go biking
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Riders cycle about wearing a few pieces of swimwear.
explanation.definitionFit: A two-piece swimsuit consists of a top and bottom worn on the beach.

clue.text: National institution working to stop protest by yard

indicators.note: to stop means plug a gap, so the working goes into the protest

parts.note: a march is a protest
on means working, as a machine is on

explanation.surface: Police work to halt a protest near Scotland Yard against a national body.
explanation.definitionFit: A crown and royal family form a national institution in Britain.

clue.text: Overturned pot — family's table accessory

indicators.note: overturned means the word is turned round and read backwards

parts.note: a pan is a cooking pot
kin are family

explanation.surface: A family knocks over a pot while setting the table.
explanation.definitionFit: A cloth or paper square for wiping hands is laid on the dining table.
